Thanks again for running the demo last week. As we discussed, we want to lock the Mutual Action Plan (MAP) so your procurement and engineering teams have a clear view of timelines and the unit economics assumptions that will govern the POC. I put together a short checklist below and attached a draft MAP spreadsheet (MAP_Acme_v1.xlsx) with placeholder numbers — please review and flag anything off.

Quick context on assumptions we've used so far (in the spreadsheet):
- Baseline model: Open-llm-35b (quantized to 4-bit), latency SLO 150ms p95 for single-request path.
- Evaluation workload: 2k avg tokens per request for batch scoring, 600 avg tokens for interactive chat flows used in product.
- Batching strategy: target throughput batching at 8 requests per batch for scoring path; interactive path uses adaptive batching (target batch size 3).
- Cache assumptions: prefix/KV hit rate assumed 25% for scoring (due to repeated reports), 10% for chat.
- Cost conversion: our internal estimate = ~1.1M tokens per $1 for the quantized model in Dedicated; hosted API prices may vary — see attached token-econ-summary.pdf.

2) Redwood: Run a unit-econ run with the agreed traffic profile and return a conservative tokens/$ baseline, and sensitivity to cache hit rate +/-15% — owner: Soojin / Dev; due: 2026-05-16.
3) Acme: Procurement to share required contract timeline and any PO templates — owner: Procurement; due: 2026-05-18.
4) Joint: Schedule POC demo + handoff to your SRE for network setup (VPC peering option) — owner: Karthik; due: 2026-05-21.

Team / Laura — attached the updated MAP_Acme_v1.xlsx and a short PDF with highlight numbers (token-econ-summary.pdf). Summary of our findings:

Unit-econ highlights (per our Dedicated reserved-capacity estimate):
- Baseline conversion: 1.05M tokens per $1 at our 4-bit quantized profile (model: open-llm-35b-q4).
- Scenario A (Conservative cache: scoring 25%, chat 5%): effective tokens/$ = 0.90M (after accounting for batch inefficiencies & cache misses); estimated daily cost for POC traffic = $420/day (~$12,600/month).
- Scenario B (Customer-provided cache rates: scoring 35%, chat 8%): effective tokens/$ = 1.02M; est daily cost = $370/day (~$11,100/month).
- Scenario C (Optimistic cache: scoring 45%, chat 15%): effective tokens/$ = 1.18M; est daily cost = $315/day (~$9,450/month).

Assumptions and sensitivity:
- Batch sizing: scoring path assumes batching size 8 (amortizes KV overhead; increases throughput, slight p95 increase ~+30-50ms). Interactive uses adaptive batching target 3 (keeps p95 under 250ms in our internal tests).
- Quantization tradeoffs: q4 gives ~2.3x cost reduction over fp16 with <1.5% mean quality delta on our evals; fallback plan is q8 for sensitive prompts.
- Warm KV/prefix cache: we modeled a 60ms saved compute per cache hit; if cache hit rate falls below 15% for scoring, costs rise ~18% in our model.
- Hosted vs Dedicated: hosted per-token price is ~10-15% higher for small POCs; recommend Dedicated Reserved if Acme expects >$80k/year spend or needs isolation.

MAP updates (short):
- Redwood: Deliver final benchmark run (with real logs) by 2026-05-19. Attachment: MAP_Acme_v1.xlsx (contains milestone table + owner list).
- Acme: Confirm LOI by 2026-05-20 and PO target 2026-06-01.
- Joint: Tech deep-dive (SRE + network) scheduled 2026-05-22 10:00 PT.

Please let me know if you want more conservative guardrails (e.g., pick q8, increase batch size) or if we should include automatic fallback to a cheaper model for non-critical requests (saves ~22%).
